correctness.rationale: Positive elements of c × R^(A\B) have a positive coordinate; a sufficiently small positive singleton indicator from C(A_infty) lies below that coordinate, proving order density and hence regularity. For y0=(0,1_(A\B)), any subordinate image vanishes on B and thus at infinity; continuity on one-point compactification implies support countable (countable union of finite level sets). Countably many such supports cannot cover uncountable A\B, excluding increasing-sequence supremum y0. The completion c-factor has decreasing tail-one sequence with coordinatewise inf0 and supnorm1, so loses sigma-Lebesgue; for X, an order-decreasing sequence to zero is pointwise decreasing to zero even at infinity (uncountable cofinite-intersection argument), then Dini yields uniform convergence and hence original q and q_a convergence.
